literal: If oneself indeed protects, anger let one restrain; if not restrained, oneself indeed will destroy, anger.
translation: If you wish to protect yourself, restrain your anger; if you do not restrain it, that very anger will destroy you.
modern: ஒருவன் தன்னைத் தான் காத்துக் கொள்ள விரும்பினால், தன் கோபத்தைக் கட்டுப்படுத்திக் காக்க வேண்டும்; அவ்வாறு காக்காவிட்டால், அந்தக் கோபமே அவனை அழித்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the self-destructive nature of anger. The author advises that if a person wishes to protect their own well-being, the primary thing they must guard against is their own anger ('cinam'). The conditional 'kākkiṉ' (if one protects) is paired with the imperative 'kākka' (let one restrain), emphasizing that self-preservation is directly tied to anger management. If one fails to do so ('kāvākkāl'), the anger does not just harm others; it turns inward and destroys ('kollum') the very person ('taṉṉaiyē') who harbors it.
